simple.meaning: יִשְׂחָק (Yischâq) is a Hebrew word meaning “Jischak , the heir of Abraham.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: יִשְׂחָק (H3446) appears 4 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Psalms 105:9, with occurrences in Psalms, Jeremiah, Amos.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יִשְׂחָק (H3446) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in יִשְׂחָק (H3446) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: יִשְׂחָק (Yischâq) / H3446 is traced through Psalms 105:9, Jeremiah 33:26, Amos 7:9, Amos 7:16 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

firstOccurrence.englishText: the covenant which he made with Abraham,

timeline.evidenceText: the covenant which he made with Abraham,

then I will also cast away the offspring of Jacob, and of David my servant, so that I will not take of his offspring to be rulers over the offspring of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: for I will cause their captivity to be reversed and will have mercy on them.”
The high places of Isaac will be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel will be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.”
Now therefore listen to Yahweh’s word: ‘You say, Don’t prophesy against Israel, and don’t preach against the house of Isaac.’
